hints: Look at the carbon skeletons and notice that the nitrile carbon becomes the alcohol carbon, so think about what intermediate links a nitrile to a primary alcohol.
Recall that acid hydrolysis of a nitrile with HCl(aq) gives a carboxylic acid, so compound X here must be propanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$.
Consider which reducing agent is strong enough to reduce a carboxylic acid all the way to a primary alcohol, and which only works on aldehydes and ketones.
walkthrough:
**Identify the starting material and product**

Great start, let's count carbons together. The starting material is propanenitrile, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C}\equiv\text{N}$, and the final product is propan-1-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$. Both have 3 carbons, so the nitrile carbon is kept and converted into the $\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ group.

**Work out step 1 to make compound X**

Nitriles are hydrolysed by heating with aqueous acid to give carboxylic acids. Here:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C}\equiv\text{N} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{HCl(aq)} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH} + \text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$$
So compound X is propanoic acid. Alkaline hydrolysis with $\text{NaOH(aq)}$ would give the carboxylate salt, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COO}^-\text{Na}^+$, which is not as useful for the next reduction.

**Work out step 2 to make the alcohol**

Carboxylic acids need a very strong reducing agent to become primary alcohols. $\text{LiAlH}_4$ (lithium aluminium hydride, in dry ether) does this reduction:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH} \xrightarrow{\text{LiAlH}_4} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$$
$\text{H}_2$ + Ni is for other reductions like alkenes or nitriles to amines, and $\text{NaBH}_4$ is too mild and only reduces aldehydes and ketones, not acids. So step 1 is HCl(aq) and step 2 is LiAlH4.

options.A: Step 1 is correct because HCl(aq) hydrolyses the nitrile to propanoic acid. However step 2 is wrong because H2 + Ni does not reduce a carboxylic acid to an alcohol. Students choosing this confuse catalytic hydrogenation with the strong hydride reduction needed for acids.
options.B: This is correct. HCl(aq) gives acid hydrolysis of propanenitrile to propanoic acid, compound X. Then LiAlH4, a powerful reducing agent, reduces the carboxylic acid to the primary alcohol propan-1-ol.
options.C: This is incorrect. NaOH(aq) gives alkaline hydrolysis to sodium propanoate, not the free acid, and H2 + Ni will not reduce a carboxylate or carboxylic acid to propan-1-ol. This traps students who remember nitrile hydrolysis but forget the acid versus base product difference.
options.D: This is incorrect on both counts for this route. NaOH(aq) gives the salt rather than the acid, and NaBH4 is too gentle to reduce carboxylic acids or carboxylates. NaBH4 only reduces aldehydes and ketones, while LiAlH4 is needed for acids.
